summary: Updates the IETF's rules on rights in contributions (RFC 3978) to say that the IETF Trust is now the proper holder of IETF-related intellectual property rights. It does not limit how the Trust uses them. This is a Best Current Practice and was replaced by RFC 5378.

plainLanguage.summary: A club used to keep its game rules in one person's care. This note says a new official keeper, the IETF Trust, now looks after them. Later the rule was rewritten again.

subtitle: Shifts IETF copyright management to a new trust organization

tldr.problem: RFC 3978 assigned IETF intellectual property rights to ISOC (Internet Society), but a new IETF Trust was created to be a better custodian of those rights.
tldr.mechanism: Updates RFC 3978 by replacing references to ISOC with the IETF Trust, making the Trust the official holder of IETF-related copyrights and IP rights.
tldr.outcome: The IETF Trust became the steward of IETF intellectual property. RFC 4748 was itself later superseded by RFC 5378.

today: RFC 4748 has been obsoleted by RFC 5378. The IETF Trust remains the custodian of IETF intellectual property rights.

sections.title: The IETF Trust
sections.content: The IETF requires authors contributing to the IETF Standards Process to grant certain rights and permissions relating to their work, documented in RFC 3978. Previously, these rights were granted to ISOC (Internet Society). However, the IETF Trust was created to act as the administrative custodian of all copyrights and intellectual property rights relating to the IETF Standards Process. This document updates RFC 3978 to recognize the IETF Trust as the proper recipient of these rights.
sections.plainLanguage: The IETF had rules about who owns the standards. A new Trust organization was created to manage ownership instead of the old Internet Society.

sections.title: The Changes
sections.content: RFC 4748 makes targeted edits to RFC 3978, replacing instances of "ISOC" and "Internet Society" with "IETF Trust and the IETF" throughout the document. Specifically, the license-grant path changes: authors now grant licenses directly to the IETF Trust rather than to ISOC. The updates affect the Introduction, sections on rights grants, authorization, copyright statements, and other provisions that reference the copyright holder. The document does not alter the underlying rights and permissions required from authors; it only changes who holds them.
sections.plainLanguage: The memo changes the rule book from "give rights to the Internet Society" to "give rights to the IETF Trust". Everything else stays the same.

sections.title: Status and Succession
sections.content: RFC 4748 is a Best Current Practice document that was itself superseded by RFC 5378 in May 2008. Both documents serve the same purpose: confirming the IETF Trust as the holder of IETF intellectual property. The IETF Trust does not constrain how it exercises those rights, allowing flexibility in licensing and reuse of IETF standards.
sections.plainLanguage: This memo updated the rules and later got replaced with a new version. The important part is that the Trust owns IETF intellectual property.
